protocol.decisive_method: exhaustive X-codeword enumeration (CP-SAT, completeness certified by OPTIMAL) plus exact GF(2) coset-budget tests against the pure-Z subgroup
protocol.coefficient_space: 132 recorded independent published rows H_B; c -> c H_B is bijective
protocol.closure_functionals: physical h in F2^288 annihilating found v, pulled back as f=H_B h

results.basis_definition: H_B = H[basis_row_indices] in the listed order

theorem_gate.question: exists v in rowspace(H) with symplectic weight <= 7 and nonzero X-part

decisive_decomposition.method: exhaustive structural decomposition (X-codeword enumeration + exact coset test)
decisive_decomposition.argument: every stabilizer is (u H_X | u P + s) with s in the pure-Z subgroup, so a weight<=w element with nonzero X-part exists iff some nonzero X-codeword x of weight <= w admits an s leaving at most w - |x| Z-support outside supp(x)

monolithic_crosscheck.reason: monolithic single-query CP-SAT run only on the benchmark member; the exhaustive decomposition decides every member

7.closure_argument: theorem gate INFEASIBLE at w=7 gives V_7 <= pure-Z subgroup, so rank(V_7) <= r_Zsub = 66; the published rows of weight <= 7 span rank 66, so rank(V_7) = 66 exactly
